title: Iran Taunts Trump With Akshay Kumar Meme After Capturing US Drone
excerpt: Tehran's embassies mocked Washington over the seizure of an unmanned US submersible in the Strait of Hormuz, while a Bollywood meme taunted Trump over $100 oil and the US midterms.
body:
• Firstpost's Vantage reported that Iran mocked US President Donald Trump with a Bollywood meme featuring actor Akshay Kumar, taunting him over oil crossing $100 a barrel and the looming US midterm elections.
  • The meme offensive followed the IRGC's capture of an unmanned US submarine at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday; Iranian state media identified the vessel as an Anduril Dive-LD autonomous drone.
  • Iranian embassies amplified the mockery on X: the mission in Ghana joked the drone was "picked it up like a plastic bottle in a fishing net," while the Hyderabad mission teased an "unboxing ceremony" by its reverse engineers.
  • The Pentagon said the drone malfunctioned more than a day earlier and was an older model carrying no sensitive data; Reuters said it could not independently verify Iran's claims.

Iran has folded Bollywood into its wartime information campaign against the United States, mocking President Donald Trump with a meme built around actor Akshay Kumar — even as its Revolutionary Guards paraded a captured American underwater drone before state cameras.

The Meme: Akshay Kumar vs. Trump

According to Firstpost's Vantage, anchored by Hem Kaur Saroya, the meme asks Trump how his war is going now that oil has crossed $100 a barrel and the US midterm elections are around the corner. It is a taunt calibrated to the two things Tehran believes hurt Trump most: energy prices and the November vote.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=iJW2qiGWpWA

A Captured Drone Becomes a Trophy

On Tuesday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its navy had captured a US uncrewed submarine at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz in what it called a complex intelligence and operational mission. Iranian state media identified the vessel as a Dive-LD, a 19-foot autonomous underwater vehicle built by California defence firm Anduril, designed for mine countermeasures, seabed mapping and the inspection of underwater infrastructure including cables and pipelines.

The IRGC Navy declared it had "trapped one of the most modern, intelligent and unmanned submarines of the terrorist American army at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz," adding that the submersible "is equipped with the latest technologies."

Washington pushed back. A Pentagon spokesperson said the underwater drone had "malfunctioned more than a day ago" while surveying regional waters in support of ongoing operations, describing it as an older model that "neither collected sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment." Reuters said it could not independently verify Iran's claims.

"Our guys picked it up like a plastic bottle in a fishing net. Fully intact. Still blinking like an idiot. Condolences to whoever was holding the joystick."

— Iran's embassy in Ghana, on X, mocking the US drone seizure

Embassy Trolling Goes Global

Iranian embassies around the world joined the mockery, according to Reuters. The mission in Ghana boasted on X that the vessel was picked up in "a strait controlled by people who can hear a shrimp sneeze." The embassy in Hyderabad wrote: "Unboxing ceremony by our reverse engineers, tomorrow morning!"

Analysts told Reuters that Iran will almost certainly attempt to reverse-engineer the drone — Tehran has done it before, unveiling domestically produced models after capturing the RQ-170 Sentinel stealth drone in 2011 — but that the episode is chiefly a propaganda victory for Tehran and an awkward setback for Washington's projection of technological superiority. "Of course Iran will take every opportunity as a propaganda win," said Farzin Nadimi, a senior fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy.

Oil, Elections and an Escalating War

The taunts land against a grim backdrop. The US-Israeli war on Iran, which began in February, has sent oil prices above $100 a barrel — a major liability for Trump and the Republicans heading into the November midterms, as Reuters reported this week. Trump has been threatening strikes on Iran's fortified Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site, warning Tehran "not to get cute." Fighting around the Strait of Hormuz — the waterway carrying a large share of the world's oil — has intensified, with both sides imposing blockades.

Bollywood as Geopolitical Currency

For Indian audiences, the episode is a striking measure of Hindi cinema's global cultural reach: Iranian state messaging reached for an Akshay Kumar meme to needle an American president. Vantage, which covers world events through an Indian lens, is watched by a large diaspora audience — and the image of Bollywood iconography circulating as wartime propaganda will be noted far beyond box-office weekends.

What to Watch

Whether Iran's promised "unboxing ceremony" produces an actual reverse-engineering showcase, and whether the tit-for-tat at Hormuz stays below the threshold of a wider escalation that would send energy prices — and the political stakes — higher still.
